Also, asking for the list isn't the answer. Asking yourself what you can do to show up for survivors, that's the answer. October 2022 will be 5yrs since the resurgence of @TaranaBurke's #MeToo, how will you show up for victims of violence? 
https://t.co/T74Aalz7PE

Dear reporters: Next month marks 5yrs since the Weinstein story broke and the resurgence Of #MeToo. If you’re writing a story, or stories, please center and lift up survivors. We are here, we are everywhere. If you want to talk through story ideas, just call me. I’m here for you.

On October 16th, 2017 as #MeToo was overflowing the internet, I was reporting to the NYPD and having a rape kit done. These 5yr reflective pieces can be hard, talking about metrics of success and KPIs may not be the way. It’s our stories, our survival.
https://t.co/8Ib2kaD5Nb

Pieces like this, where writers attempt to hold a yardstick to #MeToo, are not helpful. I want to see less talk of KPIs and metrics of success of #MeToo and more focus on the survivors and victims who are working behind the scenes to make this world better, changing the systems.
